tagline: Home of Bueng Phlan Chai, the great Phra Maha Chedi Chai Mongkol, and the Thung Kula Ronghai plains
introHtml: Roi Et sits in the middle of Isan, best known for the Ho Wot 101 observation tower rising over Bueng Phlan Chai lake in the heart of town, and the big white-and-gold Phra Maha Chedi Chai Mongkol out in Nong Phok district. The town is laid out in a ring around Bueng Phlan Chai, so you can walk the lakeside, make merit at Wat Burapha Phiram, then drift between cafes and the evening market without rushing. Out past the city is Thung Kula Ronghai, the plain that grows some of the country's most famous jasmine rice. Roi Et also holds its annual Bun Phawet merit festival every March. It's a place you can visit for the culture, the Isan food, or just an easy stroll around town.
bestTime: November–February, cool and pleasant for walking around town; if you're here for the merit festival, come in March for Bun Phawet

highlights.name: Ho Wot 101 and Bueng Phlan Chai
highlights.blurb: A tall observation tower shaped like a wot (a reed pipe) on the edge of Bueng Phlan Chai, with 360-degree views over town. The lake itself is a water park where locals come to walk and exercise every evening.

highlights.name: Phra Maha Chedi Chai Mongkol
highlights.blurb: A huge white-and-gold chedi on a hill in Nong Phok district, a place to make merit and take in the view over the Phu Khiao range — one of the first things people picture when they think of Roi Et.

highlights.name: Wat Burapha Phiram and Phra Phuttha Rattana Mongkol Maha Muni
highlights.blurb: A temple in the center of town with a very tall standing Buddha you can spot from far off. It's one of the province's key temples and a place locals come to pray.

highlights.name: Thung Kula Ronghai
highlights.blurb: A wide plain spreading across several districts of the province, famous for its jasmine rice. In early winter the fields turn lush green — a good place to stop and see rural life.

highlights.name: Bun Phawet Festival
highlights.blurb: The province's big merit festival, held every March, with the Phra Wet Sandon procession, the Maha Chat sermon, and a long painted Phawet cloth that the whole town turns out for.

highlights.name: Thung Kula jasmine rice
highlights.blurb: Jasmine rice grown on the Thung Kula plain within the province — fragrant and soft once cooked, and a well-known thing people buy to take home as a gift.

foodScene.name: Isan food
foodScene.note: Som tam, larb, koi, grilled chicken, bamboo-shoot soup — bold flavors you'll find all over town and what locals eat day to day.

foodScene.name: Thung Kula jasmine rice
foodScene.note: Quality jasmine rice from the Thung Kula plain in the province — fragrant and soft when cooked, eaten with larb and koi or bought to take home.

foodScene.name: Sticky rice and khao jee
foodScene.note: Steamed sticky rice goes with every meal, while khao jee — sticky rice brushed with egg and grilled over a fire — is a morning snack at the markets.

foodScene.name: Freshwater fish and koi pla
foodScene.note: Fish from local waters turned into koi, larb pla, and tom yum — homegrown dishes you'll find at Isan eateries around the province.

foodScene.name: Seasonal mushrooms and wild greens
foodScene.note: In the rainy season, wild mushrooms and foraged greens from the fields show up at the fresh markets, cooked into Isan-style curries and soups.

foodScene.name: Mu kratha and casual evening spots
foodScene.note: Mu kratha (DIY grill-and-hotpot) is a popular dinner here, with plenty of spots to choose from around Bueng Phlan Chai and the town center.

foodScene.name: Cafes in town
foodScene.note: The town center has plenty of small new cafes — an easy place to sit with a coffee while you're walking around Bueng Phlan Chai.

foodScene.name: Evening market and street food
foodScene.note: The evening market in the center brings together Isan snacks and street food to graze on after dark, at local prices.

attractions.name: Ho Wot 101
attractions.blurb: A tall observation tower shaped like a wot on the edge of Bueng Phlan Chai. Take the lift up for 360-degree views over Roi Et, with a glass floor for anyone feeling brave.

attractions.name: Bueng Phlan Chai
attractions.blurb: A public park on the water in the heart of town and the symbol of Roi Et, with an island in the middle, the city pillar shrine, and a path around the lake where locals come to exercise.

attractions.name: Phra Maha Chedi Chai Mongkol
attractions.blurb: A huge white-and-gold chedi on a hill in Nong Phok district. Walk through the artwork inside, then head up for views over the Phu Khiao range around it.

attractions.name: Wat Burapha Phiram
attractions.blurb: A temple in the center of town with a very tall standing Buddha you can see from far off — an important temple and a place locals come to pray.

attractions.name: Roi Et National Museum
attractions.blurb: A museum in the center of town covering the province's history, art, and local woven textiles — a good stop to get to know Roi Et.

attractions.name: Ku Ka Sing
attractions.blurb: A Khmer stone sanctuary in Kaset Wisai district, a trace of old civilization out on the Thung Kula plain, where you can walk among the ancient sandstone architecture.

attractions.name: Bueng Kluea (the Isan sea)
attractions.blurb: A wide lake in Selaphum district with a sandy shore to sit and relax by — locals call it the Isan sea.

attractions.name: Thung Kula Ronghai
attractions.blurb: A wide expanse of rice fields in the province, famous for its jasmine rice. In early winter the fields turn lush green — a good place to stop for photos and a look at rural Isan life.
